summary: This article explains how the heart pumps blood around the body, why it beats faster during exercise, and how being active every day makes it stronger.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Exercise and Your Heart” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: a gas in the air that people and animals need to breathe and stay alive
a tube in the body that carries blood
the beat you can feel when your heart pushes blood through your body

challengeTerms.def: having to do with the heart and the blood vessels
to move around in a loop and come back to the start
strong, energetic, and full of effort

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that playing outside is just as important for children as doing homework? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain what happens inside your body when you start running.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review oxygen, vessel, and pulse, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses cardiovascular, circulate, and vigorous to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
